item.title: Monaghan GP says it's not too late to get flu vaccine
item.description: A Monaghan GP says that while flu numbers didn't reach the levels the HSE initially feared, hospitals are still under huge pressure. Dr. Illona Duffy said that a lot of people are still presenting with the flu and not responding or recovering from it and ending up with secondary infections. She is warning people that the flu season is not over yet, with both adults and children presenting in GP surgeries, and some still being hospitalised. item.title: Carrickmacross personal trainer on importance of fitness
item.description: A county Monaghan personal trainer says the information is there for us to listen to in terms of obesity levels in Ireland. As it stands, 60% of adults and over 1 in 5 children and young people are living with being overweight or obesity, in Ireland, one of the highest levels in Europe. Christina McMahon who is a former boxer now working in Carrickmacross, says that stress is something that can add to weight gain. item.description: World champion Luke Littler will headline a new eight-player line-up for this year's Premier League Darts. item.description: Some 390 new speed camera zones have been rolled out by gardaí in recent days as part of a campaign to reduce road deaths caused by speeding. 185 people lost their lives in 174 road crashes during 2025, compared to 171 deaths in 157 collisions in 2024, according to new figures released by the Road Safety Authority. 5 people died on Monaghan roads in 2025 and 2 people lost their lives on Cavan roads over the past 12 months. item.title: Cavan farmer elected IFA Poultry Chair
item.description: Brendan Soden, a layer farmer and pullet producer from Stradone Co. Cavan, has been elected Chair of the IFA Poultry Committee, following a meeting yesterday. Mr Soden previously served as Vice Chair. He succeeds Nigel Sweetnam, who has completed a four-year term as Chair. item.title: Blayney Blades set to celebrate Nollaig na mBan
item.description: Today, January 6th, marks Nollaig na mBan, traditionally known as Women's Little Christmas, marked on the Feast of the Epiphany. Historically in Ireland, this was a day when women were finally able to rest after the busy Christmas period. In more recent years, Nollaig na mBan has been joyfully re-introduced in many communities, often through gatherings and events that also raise funds for worthy charities - celebrating women, connection and generosity.
